title: SLO Governance: Dynamic Capacity & Fallbacks — Playbook and Rollout Plan
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines governance, decision logic, and an actionable rollout for dynamic capacity policies and multi-tier fallbacks tied to SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Goal: reduce customer-visible incidents by enabling automated, auditable fallbacks while keeping SLO ownership clear across product, serving runtime, infra, and platform teams.

Scope:
- Applies to public generation/chat endpoints, embeddings endpoints, and model-routing policies in Redwood hosted and Dedicated pools.
- Excludes low-level infra (host OS) patching cadence; includes autoscaling and model-variant fallback logic.
- Intended for services with customer-facing SLOs (latency, success-rate, correctness signals) and for internal SLOs that drive routing decisions.

Principles:
1) Explicit ownership: each SLO must have a named steward and a fallback policy attached.
2) Safe automation: automated fallbacks require automated canary verification targets and rollback paths.
3) Observable and reversible: all fallback decisions must emit events with reason, metric snapshots, and rollback token.
4) Minimal customer surprise: fallbacks degrade predictably (e.g., model-quality tier -> latency tier), not silently.

Key Terminology:
- SLO steward: owner accountable for the SLO and associated rollback decisions.
- Fallback policy: set of actions (model variant, region, capacity tier) executed when triggers fire.
- Trigger: metric-based condition evaluated by the routing/orchestration layer.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- SRE (site-reliability-engineering): policy enforcement, incident runbooks, observability; owns canary/deployment tooling (Jira SRE-4821).
- Serving Runtime: implements runtime-level fallback actions, model-variant compatibility checks (PR runtime#981).
- Platform/Infra: capacity provisioning, autoscaling policies and bare-metal/GPU pool orchestration (PLAT-3320).
- Product/Hosted API: define customer SLOs, success/quality definitions, and acceptable degradation paths.
- Customer Success: communication templates for customers impacted by tiered fallbacks.

Fallback taxonomy (examples):
- Model-Variant Fallback: auto-switch from high-quality high-latency variant (quantized fp16-qat) -> lower-cost quantized variant when cost or queue depth breach thresholds.
- Capacity Tier Fallback: move requests from Dedicated pool to Hosted pool with rate-limited burst allowance.
- Regional Fallback: route traffic to a secondary region when primary region's P99 latency > threshold for N minutes.
- Graceful Degradation: reduce max tokens, enable prefix-KV caching, or downsample safety checks to keep latency within SLOs.

Trigger matrix (sample):
- Trigger A: Endpoint P99 latency > 250ms for 3 continuous 1-minute windows -> action: enable aggressive batching and KV cache; notify steward.
- Trigger B: Request queue depth > 500 for 2 minutes or tail queue growth rate > 20%/min -> action: spin-up burst capacity + enable model-variant fallback if new capacity doesn't stabilize in 90s.
- Trigger C: Error-rate (server 5xx + inference rejects) > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes -> action: shift 20% of traffic to fallback model + open incident.

SLI / SLO examples to attach to policies:
- Latency SLO (interactive-generation): p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms over 7d window, objective: 99.9% p95 attainment.
- Success SLO (generation success): generation success-rate >= 99.5% measured as completed token streams / attempted requests over 1d window.
- Quality guardrail (semantic fidelity): regression < 1.0% vs baseline prompts (evaluated in rollout canary).

Governance & Policy Lifecycle:
1) Define SLO and attach fallback taxonomy in SLO registry page (Confluence/CONFLUENCE-12345).
2) Implement fallback automation in runtime with feature-flag gating.
3) Create a canary plan with synthetic traffic and selected customer-safe prompts. Canary must show no >1% regression on quality guardrail and maintain latency targets.
4) Schedule a staged rollout (internal -> beta customers -> general) with a cooldown window and automatic rollback conditions.

Rollout plan (high level):
- Week 0 (owner: Jordan Park): Finalize policy spec, identify stewards for 8 critical endpoints.
- Week 1 (owner: Serving Runtime): Implement noop policy endpoints + feature flag (runtime#981).
- Week 2 (owner: SRE): Wire triggers into alerting and event stream; create dashboards.
- Week 3 (owner: Platform): Allocate burst pools and configure autoscaler profiles (ticket PLAT-3320).
- Week 4–5: Canary testing (internal), run chaos scenarios (traffic spike, GPU OOM), validate canary metrics.
- Week 6: Beta pilot for 3 low-risk customers, monitor for 7 days.
- Week 8: Full rollout with gradual percentage increase and automatic rollback guardrails.

Validation & Testing:
- Synthetic traffic harness: run 6-hour spike test that emulates production distribution (p95/p99/queue depth).
- Quality canary set: curated 200 prompt set across customers; measure model-answer similarity and hallucination metrics.
- Chaos tests: simulate region outage by dropping 10% of primary region hosts and confirm routing triggers.
- Regression criteria: any canary where quality metric regression > 1% or latency degradation > 10% -> block rollout.

Observability requirements:
- Dashboards: per-endpoint SLI view (p50/p95/p99, success-rate, queue depth, active instances).
- Events: every fallback decision must write an event to event-bus and include: timestamp, endpoint, SLO id, trigger, action, metric snapshot, steward.
- Audit: store fallback events for 90 days; keep week-over-week snapshot to review policy effectiveness.

Runbooks & Escalation:
- Automated rollback: if fallback causes quality regression beyond threshold, system must revert within 3 minutes and page SLO steward + SRE on-call.
- Manual escalation play: 1) Page steward, 2) Open incident in SRE-bridge, 3) If no response in 10 minutes escalate to Eng Director.
- Post-incident: 72-hour retro and follow-up action with assigned owner and SLA to close.

Operational guardrails (acceptance criteria):
- Policies must be feature-flagged and reversible.
- All triggers must have documented thresholds, data sources, and owners in Confluence.
- No blind routing to unknown model variants; every variant must be validated against a compatibility matrix.
- Tests automated in CI for policy engine with mocked metrics.

Communication plan:
- Internal: weekly status update to #sre-model-serving and a standing 30-minute sync during rollout.
- Customer-facing: templates for CS to notify affected customers in beta and full rollout; include opt-out link for Dedicated customers.

Dependencies & Open tickets:
- PLAT-3320: Burst pool configuration and autoscaler profiles (platform).
- SRE-4821: Canary automation and alert binding (SRE).
- runtime#981: runtime feature-flag and policy API changes (serving runtime).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Quality tolerance for model-variant fallback for enterprise customers (opt-in vs forced).
- Billing implications when moving Dedicated -> Hosted during fallbacks. Need finance/legal input.
- How to expose fallback events in tenant audit logs for private deployments.

Next steps (short):
- [ ] Assign stewards for remaining 12 endpoints (owner: Jordan Park, due 2026-02-20).
- [ ] Finalize trigger thresholds with product (due 2026-02-24).
- [ ] Implement event schema and wire to event-bus (SRE-4821).
- [ ] Add canary prompt set into test harness and run baseline (Serving Runtime + QA).

Appendix: sample SLO entry to attach to registry (copy/paste)
- SLO ID: SLO-GEN-012
- Endpoint: /v1/generate-chat
- SLI definitions: p99 latency measured at LB (ingress) over 24h; success-rate = completed streams/requests (exclude client disconnect).
- SLO: p99 < 300ms 99.5% of time (30d rolling), success-rate >= 99.5 daily.
- Fallback policy: 1) enable kv-prefix cache, 2) model-variant fallback to gen-medium-quantized, 3) regional spill to eu-west-1 if primary latency > 400ms for 10m.
- Steward: Asha Patel
- Runbook link: CONFLUENCE-12345

Document owner/next contact: Jordan Park (jordan.park@redwood.ai)
